subject: plab-dermatology
title: Eczema and dermatitis: barrier defect, stepped topical therapy, allergy

steps.tx: **Atopic eczema** is a chronic relapsing inflammatory dermatosis characterized by severe pruritus and impaired epidermal barrier function, frequently linked to loss-of-function filaggrin gene mutations. Lesions show age-dependent distributions: facial and extensor surfaces in infants, shifting to flexural folds such as antecubital and popliteal fossae in older children and adults.
steps.say: Atopic eczema causes intense pruritus and barrier breakdown, affecting flexural creases in older children and adults.

steps.tx: **Emollient therapy** forms the indispensable foundation of all atopic eczema management. Liberal, frequent application of greasy leave-on emollients restores stratum corneum hydration and reinforces defective lipid lamellae. Emollients should be applied smoothly in the direction of hair growth several times daily, continuing faithfully even during complete disease quiescence.
steps.say: Liberal, frequent emollients form the mandatory foundation, applied along hair growth to rebuild stratum corneum hydration.

rows: Stepped potency, match to anatomical site
Face and flexures, avoids skin atrophy

steps.tx: **Topical corticosteroids** are stepped in potency according to flare severity and anatomical vulnerability. Mild formulations such as hydrocortisone are reserved for delicate facial and intertriginous skin to avert telangiectasia and dermal atrophy. Moderate to potent preparations are utilized for thickened lichenified plaques on limbs and trunk.
steps.say: Use mild steroids on the face and flexures to prevent atrophy. Reserve potent steroids for lichenified trunk and limb plaques.

vis.caption: Topical corticosteroid potency by body region.

steps.tx: **Contact dermatitis** divides into irritant and allergic subtypes. Irritant contact dermatitis is a non-immunological physical or chemical disruption affecting anyone exposed to sufficient wet work, detergents or solvents. Allergic contact dermatitis represents a Type IV delayed hypersensitivity reaction to specific haptens like nickel, fragrance, or chromate, requiring diagnostic patch testing.
steps.say: Irritant dermatitis results from direct chemical barrier damage. Allergic dermatitis is Type IV hypersensitivity, confirmed by patch testing.

steps.tx: **Venous stasis eczema** affects the gaiter region of the lower legs secondary to chronic venous hypertension and valvular incompetence. Progressive extravasation of red blood cells causes haemosiderin pigmentation and chronic subcutaneous fibrosis termed lipodermatosclerosis. Graduated compression hosiery is curative, provided peripheral arterial disease is excluded with an ankle-brachial pressure index.
steps.say: Venous stasis eczema affects the gaiter area with haemosiderin and lipodermatosclerosis. Compression requires an ABPI above point eight.
